I ran an initial pass on the CSV and logs. Quick notes (see attached investigation-notes-20261129.txt):
- IP overlap: two of the accounts originate from the same /24 subnet and a third from a nearby ASN used by the same ISP in the region.
- Payment instruments: card fingerprints show partial overlap; one card token appears on two accounts in the past 30 days.
- Email domains: one account uses alex@skyline-sys.com, another uses billing+us@skyline-sys.com; the third uses a personal gmail (likely a test alias).
- Time clustering: three top-ups within 90 minutes, all for the same dollar amount.

Recommendation: classify as "probable coordinated top-ups" pending procurement proof. Place temporary hold on further credits for all Skyline-related accounts, and schedule reversal of the last two auto-topups pending approvals. Also recommend a short call with the customer to request PO and SSO mapping.

If legal/finance wants to push back, note that we have credit reversal precedent in our policy for suspected multi-account abuse.
